body:
Chief: RUNNING MY OWN CORRECTED HEURISTIC FOUND TWO MORE, AND A HOLE IN MY SLICE PLAN. This is the follow-through the AuthorizedRemoteRequest correction implied, and it paid twice.

I searched for the shape my original ranking was blind to: a private constructor with NO COMPANION OBJECT, meaning the type is gated by something else entirely. Twelve across the repo. Two of them are the same class as AuthorizedRemoteRequest, and again THE SCALADOC STATES THE GUARANTEE THAT fromProduct BREAKS:

CheckedSidecarPrelude - "A VERIFIED SM4SFT02 header and digest index rooted in the manifest's index checksum. Why: individual block checks are trustworthy only after the small prelude has been VERIFIED AGAINST EVIDENCE THAT DID NOT COME FROM THE SIDECAR FILE ITSELF."

CheckedSidecarBlock - "One INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED SM4SFT02 block decoded at its global compact-row position. Why: A PARTIAL FETCH MUST NEVER MASQUERADE AS VALIDATION of the complete sidecar or a fully materialized FeatureTrack."

Both are minted only by 'new Checked...' inside a for-comprehension behind the verifying gate, at sidecar.scala:537 and :573. Both are case classes with private[codec] constructors, so both have a public fromProduct. The entire purpose of these two types is to be a WITNESS that verification happened against external evidence - and one line mints a witness that witnessed nothing. The second type's doc says a partial fetch must never masquerade as validation; forging one is exactly that masquerade.

THE HOLE IN MY PLAN, which is worse than the finding. CODEC IS NOT IN MY SLICE PLAN AT ALL. I scoped five slices covering view, core, align, document, acquire, interview, features, embed-grakern and embed-core - and codec appears nowhere, because these three types never entered my 45-item "validating" list, because they have no self-validating companion, because of the same heuristic that mis-ranked AuthorizedRemoteRequest. The flaw did not just misorder the work; IT DELETED A MODULE FROM IT.

THE BETTER RULE, which I am adopting and writing onto the parent bead: A TYPE WHOSE NAME IS AN ASSERTION IS THE WORST ONE TO LEAVE FORGEABLE. Checked-, Authorized-, Validated-, -Receipt, -Proof, -Witness. These types exist for no purpose other than to carry a claim that something was verified, and they are precisely the ones a self-validation heuristic cannot see, because their verification is by construction somewhere else. Forging a ValidatedVector corrupts arithmetic; forging a CheckedSidecarPrelude or an AuthorizedRemoteRequest defeats a check we built deliberately and then documented as impossible to bypass.

ADDING SLICE 6 - codec: CheckedSidecarPrelude (sidecar.scala:329), CheckedSidecarBlock (:341), SidecarBlockRange (:221). And I am re-checking the other nine externally-gated types for the same shape - align's StructuralReductionReceipt is a Receipt built by wire.scala and gets the same scrutiny.

I have now made the same class of error twice in one hour: trusting a mechanical filter to rank work whose importance is semantic. Both times the fix was to read the type's own documentation, which stated the guarantee plainly. The grep tells you what a type IS; the Scaladoc tells you what it PROMISES, and it is the promise that matters when deciding what a forged instance costs.
